appended_meaning:
The materially referenced health-funding availability and disclosure conditions are compared at complete sections 501, 502 and 505 in each original requirements Act: PL113-235 division G 2015, PL115-31 division H 2017, PL116-94 division A 2020 and PL117-328 division H 2023. The established section 3 rule keeps each this-Act reference within its own division unless expressly provided otherwise. These remain requirements-source conditions invoked through the literal health-transfer reference chain; their original years, dated source/amendment periods and exact EH continuing direction are retained, rather than silently replaced with one present-year or individual application.

Complete section 501 authorizes the Secretaries of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education to transfer unexpended balances of prior appropriations to accounts corresponding to current appropriations provided in that Act/division. This is an authorized transfer of existing balances, not a new appropriation, a mandatory transfer or permission to move every balance to any account. Transferred balances must be used for the same purpose and the same periods of time for which they were originally appropriated. Both original-purpose and original-period constraints remain; the source does not reset the funds' life or declare an actual balance, transfer, expenditure or program award.

Complete section 502 provides that no part of an appropriation contained in that Act/division remains available for obligation beyond the current fiscal year unless expressly so provided therein. The express-exception predicate remains part of the condition. This is an obligation-availability rule, not proof that all such funds expire on one common date, a change to every prior appropriation's purpose/period or a finding that funds were actually obligated or spent. The established assessment-funded medical transfer's until-expended language and other express source availability provisions are retained. Their exact interaction with dated incorporated requirements and continuing direction is not converted here into a categorical current-grant expiry or a blanket override.

Complete section 505 applies to all grantees receiving Federal funds included in the Act/division, including but not limited to State/local governments and Federal research-grant recipients, when they issue the specified documents describing projects or programs funded in whole or in part with Federal money. The trigger covers statements, press releases, requests for proposals, bid solicitations and other such documents. Whole-or-part funding, grantee receipt of the covered funds, document issuance and project/program-description scope remain together; this is not every person's conversation, every private project or a new immigration-status test.

For those documents, the grantee must clearly state the percentage of total project/program costs financed with Federal money, the dollar amount of Federal funds for the project/program, and both the percentage and dollar amount of total costs financed by non-governmental sources. Federal share percentage and dollar amount remain distinct, and the non-governmental disclosure keeps both measures. Non-governmental is not silently changed to all non-Federal sources, every State/local contribution or an invented matching-fund requirement. No actual allocation, recipient compliance, undisclosed financing, misuse or motive is inferred.

All four Acts contain matching operative 501/502/505 clauses at this selected extent, after a private comparison removes only original notes and page markers. Original source bytes, glyphs, annotations, page markers, division identities and years remain unchanged; no source-year scope is erased by the comparison. These are context for the whole H.R. 1968 passage choice, without assigning a separate balance-transfer/disclosure stance or four additional actions to either member. The earlier needle-program version difference remains preserved, as do medical/grant/child-service qualifications, shared compacts, recorded choices, counting, eligibility and the compiled proposition graph.

This completes only the selected transfer, availability and funding-disclosure provisions. Other materially relevant program, HHS and general requirements, substantive cross-references, exact carry-forward/current application and remaining package authorities remain executable research. Unfinished research is not unavailable evidence. All 70 separate application questions, including frozen Q68/Q69/Q70, remain unchanged. No full conditions/fund/package/domain closure, independent acceptance, production eligibility or publication is declared.

SEC. 3. <<NOTE: 1 USC 1 note.>> REFERENCES. Except as expressly provided otherwise, any reference to ``this Act'' contained in any division of this Act shall be treated as referring only to the provisions of that division. 

DIVISION G--DEPARTMENTS <<NOTE: Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2015. Department of Labor Appropriations Act, 2015.>> OF LABOR, HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, AND EDUCATION, AND RELATED AGENCIES APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2015 

Sec. 506. (a) None of the funds appropriated in this Act, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are appropriated in this Act, shall be expended for any abortion. (b) None of the funds appropriated in this Act, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are appropriated in this Act, shall be expended for health benefits coverage that includes coverage of abortion. (c) The term ``health benefits coverage'' means the package of services covered by a managed care provider or organization pursuant to a contract or other arrangement. Sec. 507. (a) The limitations established in the preceding section shall not apply to an abortion-- (1) if the pregnancy is the result of an act of rape or incest; or (2) in the case where a woman suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness, including a life-endangering physical condition caused by or arising from the pregnancy itself, that would, as certified by a physician, place the woman in danger of death unless an abortion is performed. (b) Nothing in the preceding section shall be construed as prohibiting the expenditure by a State, locality, entity, or private person of State, local, or private funds (other than a State's or locality's contribution of Medicaid matching funds). (c) Nothing in the preceding section shall be construed as restricting the ability of any managed care provider from offering abortion coverage or the ability of a State or locality to contract separately with such a provider for such coverage with State funds (other than a State's or locality's contribution of Medicaid matching funds). (d)(1) None of the funds made available in this Act may be made available to a Federal agency or program, or to a State or local government, if such agency, program, or government subjects any institutional or individual health care entity to discrimination on the basis that the health care entity does not provide, pay for, provide coverage of, or refer for abortions. (2) In this subsection, the term ``health care entity'' includes an individual physician or other health care professional, a hospital, a provider-sponsored organization, a health maintenance organization, a health insurance plan, or any other kind of health care facility, organization, or plan.
